findings.reason: the plan must name these two owners and state each one's disposition — route it through the hoisted expression/derivation, or keep it with a reason — otherwise the consolidation its done-when asserts is neither complete nor checkable, which is the same hand-written-list undercount §17 itself says every prior review of this design produced.
findings.text: §16 fixes the shared section-spelling expression by enumerating "Four grammars recognise a section spelling today" (routing's _SECTION_IDENTITY, ledger.normalize_section, evidence._section_key, doccheck._NUMBERED_SECTION_ID) and §17's done-when greps the package for section-spelling regular expressions "and requires that one", but two further sites recognise or emit section identities and appear in neither enumeration: reckon/_store.py:1779 compiles re.compile(r"^s[0-9]+$") inline inside _require_new_section_contracts (a narrower full-match numbering grammar of the same shape as doccheck's, which §16 does route through the derivation), and reckon/roadmap.py:170 compiles _SECTION_WORD_RE whose matches at roadmap.py:253 bind gate-text references into f"s{int(number)}" identities. The plan's stated count of four, its "which grammar wins is stated here" rule, and its claim that ledger and evidence are "otherwise unchanged" are therefore incomplete, and §17's one-expression done-when is in tension with them.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 hides raw-text section span, heading level, identity, extent, card recognition and machinery-element recognition behind one private parser plus a small set of shared predicates on reckon/_plan_html.py, and §16 collapses the whole-document fingerprint into a per-section digest map behind one module-private helper; no new module family of shallow wrappers is introduced.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the section-spelling grammar the plan consolidates has two more owners than §16 names, in reckon/_store.py:1779 and reckon/roadmap.py:170.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 states no public definition is added and retires plan_fingerprint's public `legacy` flag, §17 names its two additions and the landed_section_ids move, and §18 names its one addition and the RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX move, so every section that adds surface accounts for it against the family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan opens the code it would extend and cites the owner of each mechanism it extends (the span parser and record reader in reckon/_plan_html.py, section_record_id/section_id_candidates in reckon/crew/routing.py, landed_section_ids in reckon/_store.py, the AST census read_trees/definitions in reckon/interface_counts.py, list_plan_reviews in reckon/crew/plan_review.py), so the reuse map is present and machine-checked by grep done-whens.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the single new public accessor, plan_headings, is justified in §17's own text (the parser is shared by five consumers across a package boundary and must stay private), and each new predicate replaces three existing spellings of one test rather than forwarding to a single existing caller, so no wrapper lacks its "why not extend" reason.
